title: agent_improvement_candidate/v1
description: Schema for a single improvement candidate proposed by an agent-retrospective run. candidate_status is a closed enum whose transitions are constrained by the state machine in validate_retrospective_schema.py (ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS / validate_transition()), not merely by this schema's enum. Per ADR 0007 Decision 4 (mutation boundary), transitioning a candidate to 'accepted' and beyond, and creating an implementation issue, are remediation / control-plane mutations that require prior explicit human authorization; this schema only describes the shape of a candidate record, it does not itself perform or authorize any mutation. `finding_contract` (Issue #2288) is an additive, optional versioned envelope: when absent, the record is a legacy lifecycle-only candidate with no delta-evaluation capability (delta_capability: legacy_unavailable, see compute_delta_capability() in validate_retrospective_schema.py -- this schema does not itself store a delta_capability field, nor does it auto-generate or backfill finding_contract.identity for legacy records). When present, finding_contract's internal keys (schema_version/identity/claim_class/evaluations) are all-or-none required by its own nested schema -- partial envelopes are rejected. candidate_id (this record's lifecycle identity) and finding_contract.identity (a cross-run semantic identity used to correlate the same underlying finding across separate agent-retrospective runs) are deliberately distinct identity concepts; this schema fixes candidate:finding cardinality at 1:1 (aggregating multiple findings under one candidate is out of scope).

candidate_id.description: Stable identifier for this improvement candidate.

candidate_status.description: Closed enum of candidate lifecycle states. Valid transitions between these states are enforced by validate_transition() in validate_retrospective_schema.py, not by this schema alone (e.g. 'rejected' -> 'implemented' is a value each individually valid but a transition rejected by the state machine). implementation_issue_created/implemented/validating/validated require implementation_issue_ref; rejected requires rejection_reason; superseded requires superseded_by (schema-enforced via the allOf/if/then invariants above). This lifecycle enum and its ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS graph are independent of finding_contract.evaluations[].delta_status (Issue #2288): candidate_status is never derived from, nor mutated by, delta evaluation outcomes.

title.description: Short human-readable summary of the candidate.

description.description: Full description of the proposed improvement. MUST be a schema-controlled projection (ADR 0007 Decision 6 allowlist model) -- not a raw transcript, and must not contain secrets, absolute local paths, or unredacted private GitHub content. This schema enforces the field allowlist only; value-level public-safety validation (secret/PII/path redaction) is Child 6's responsibility (ADR 0007 Decision 6, two-layer defense).

source_run_ref.description: Reference back to the agent_retrospective_run/v1 run_identity that produced this candidate.

implementation_issue_ref.description: Reference (e.g. issue number/URL) to the implementation issue. Required once candidate_status reaches implementation_issue_created or later (schema-enforced).

rejection_reason.description: Required when candidate_status is rejected (schema-enforced); explains why the candidate was not accepted.

superseded_by.description: Reference to the candidate that superseded this one. Required when candidate_status is superseded (schema-enforced).

claim_class.description: ADR 0007 Decision 2 claim-class taxonomy (exact 9-value closed enum). Used both as finding_contract.claim_class (the overall claim class of the finding) and inside finding_contract.identity.key.claim_class (one of the typed identity key components).

finding_identity.description: FINDING_IDENTITY_V1: a stable, cross-run semantic identity for a finding, deterministically derived from a typed key via compute_finding_identity()/validate_finding_identity() (validate_retrospective_schema.py). Deliberately excludes run/occurrence-varying inputs (source_run_ref, base_sha, source_set_digest, any timestamp, evidence fingerprints) so the same underlying finding keeps the same identity across separate runs.

algorithm.description: Identity digest algorithm. Fixed at v1; a future algorithm value would be a different namespace and is out of scope for this schema version.

key.description: Typed identity key. Deliberately does not include source_run_ref/base_sha/source_set_digest/timestamps/evidence fingerprints -- see compute_finding_identity().

value.description: Normalized, stable reference within `kind` (e.g. a repository-relative path, an issue/PR number, a workflow id).

"sha256:" + SHA256(canonicalized key) as computed by compute_finding_identity(). validate_finding_identity() recomputes this from `key` and rejects the candidate if the stored value does not match (stale/copied/fabricated identity).

signal.description: Typed union representing a single observed/expected signal value (baseline_signal / current_signal / expected_signal). `null` represents a legitimate absence (e.g. no baseline exists yet for a brand-new finding), and is distinct from an omitted key -- baseline_signal/current_signal/expected_signal are always present, but may be null.

value.description: Typed value; the concrete JSON type is expected to match signal_type (boolean/integer/number types map directly, 'enum' and 'digest' are represented as string).

tolerance.description: Optional numeric tolerance for comparator-based classification.

evidence_ref.description: Public-safe, typed evidence reference. Deliberately excludes any raw-evidence field (full transcript text, secrets, absolute local paths, unredacted private content) -- additionalProperties: false enforces the field allowlist; value-level redaction of resource_identity/projection_digest inputs is Issue #2239's responsibility, not this schema's.

resource_identity.description: Typed, normalized public-safe identifier (e.g. a public GitHub URL, a repository-relative path + commit SHA). MUST NOT be raw transcript text.

projection_digest.description: sha256 digest of a redacted, public-safe projection of the evidence -- not a hash of raw/private content.

evaluation.description: A single delta-evaluation event for a finding, produced by a future retrospective-evaluator (Issue #2237; this schema only defines the representation, not the computation). Five separated judgement axes (evaluation_status / presence_delta / signal_delta / delta_status / indeterminate_reason) are kept mutually exclusive per the allOf invariants below: delta_status is required iff evaluation_status is 'classified' and forbidden when 'indeterminate'; indeterminate_reason is null iff evaluation_status is 'classified' and a non-null enum value iff 'indeterminate'; incomplete source_coverage forces evaluation_status to 'indeterminate' (an indeterminate evaluation is never reported as 'resolved'); presence_delta 'recurrent' takes summary precedence over a concurrently-held signal_delta 'regressed' for delta_status (both are preserved -- delta_status='recurrent', signal_delta='regressed' -- so recurrence and regression are both representable at once).

previous_evaluation_ref.description: evaluation_id of the immediately preceding evaluation for the same finding, or null for the first evaluation. Cross-checked against evaluation history ordering by validate_finding_contract_history() (validate_retrospective_schema.py), not merely this schema's type.

observed.description: Whether the finding was observed to still be present in the current run.

delta_status.description: Backward-compatible single-enum summary of presence_delta/signal_delta. Required iff evaluation_status is 'classified'; forbidden when 'indeterminate' (an indeterminate evaluation must never be reported as 'resolved' or any other delta_status).

indeterminate_reason.description: Non-null iff evaluation_status is 'indeterminate'; null iff 'classified'.

finding_contract.description: Versioned envelope (Issue #2288). Optional at the top level (absent -> legacy lifecycle-only candidate, delta evaluation not available). When present, all of schema_version/identity/claim_class/evaluations are required (all-or-none; enforced simply by this $ref applying its own `required` list only when the `finding_contract` key itself is present).

evaluations.description: Evaluation event history, oldest first. At least one evaluation is required once finding_contract is present.
